title: Introduce controlled stormgate admission + sparse KV drain protector for safer cross-region failback
author: Priya Raman
body: Motivation: We observed a recent incident where aggressive cross-region failback caused a synchronized mass KV cache eviction which amplified latency spikes and forced repeated circuit tripping across many nodes. The root cause was (1) immediate admission of warmup and backfilled traffic during failback, and (2) an all-or-nothing KV drain that invalidated prefix caches simultaneously across replicas. This PR introduces a two-part mitigation: a lightweight admission controller called 'stormgate' that rate-moderates inflight reconnections during regional failback, and a sparse KV drain protector that staggers and limits the scope of prefix/KV invalidations to avoid correlated cache loss. This is a hotfix intended to reduce SLO violations during regional reconverge windows without requiring capacity changes. What I changed: - service/gateway/stormgate.go: new admission filter implementing a tokenized window (configurable burst and refill) tied to regional-failback state. The filter is intentionally conservative by default (window=30s, burst=50 tokens). - serving/kv/protector.go: sparse drain algorithm that selects a bounded subset of hot prefixes to drain per wave and records a drain_epoch token so other nodes avoid redundant evictions. - runtime/orchestrator: small hooks to emit telemetry events (stormgate.open/close, kv.protect.wave.{start,complete}) and to consult stormgate when orchestrating reconverge. - telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics and dashboards referenced in the rollout notes. - tests/*: unit tests for stormgate token refill, integration test simulating a two-region failback that asserts per-node prefix survival and SLO delta. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to Canary region for 2h with debug telemetry enabled. 2) If canary SLO delta <= 0.25% and no new KV evictions spike, rollout to remaining regions in waves (10% zones per 10m). 3) Monitor metrics: slo.serving.p99, stormgate.tokens, kv.protector.eviction_rate. Config knobs: stormgate.window_seconds, stormgate.burst_tokens, protector.max_prefixes_per_wave. Related incidents and tickets: INC-2024-311 (cross-region reconverge), Linked to ENG-3142 (postmortem), ENG-3199 (follow-up automation). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for algorithmic invariants - [x] Integration regression sim for small cluster - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks - [x] Docs: brief entries in runbook/regional-failback.md - [x] Manual verification run on staging Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-sized burst could cause excess throttling. Mitigation: conservative defaults + runtime flag to disable. - Risk: protector could leave stale prefixes un-evicted long-term. Mitigation: protector includes an epoch TTL and fallback that re-queues prefixes after N waves. Observability: added histogram metrics and sparse trace spans to correlate stormgate events with SLO deltas. If we see slow reopen of circuits we can increase stormgate.refill_rate temporarily. Why not simpler approaches: we considered global throttle at LB but that would hurt global latency and not target the reconverge window; coordinated KV checkpoints were heavier and risked longer outage windows. This approach is incremental and safe. Merge notes: merged via squash after one minor follow-up to tighten a race in protector requeue logic.

b22c9b1: implement sparse kv drain protector with epoch token bookkeeping
c3d9f01: wire telemetry and metrics, add dashboards
d47a8f2: integration test: simulated two-region failback
e59b0c3: fix race in protector requeue (requested by María Gómez)
diff_snippets: service/gateway/stormgate.go: new token bucket interface with context-aware TryAcquire(ctx) and reason tags
serving/kv/protector.go: ProtectWave(prefixes []string) implements bounded drain and records drain_epoch metadata on prefix keys
runtime/orchestrator/reconverge_hooks.go: consult stormgate before opening reconverge window and emit events
review_comments: Aiden Cho: Can you add a unit test that asserts tokens don't refill when region is in 'hold' state? I worry about an edge-case where tokens leak.
Priya Raman: Added a test (see commit e59b0c3) and tightened the hold-state check so refill is gated behind atomic state transition.
María Gómez: Protector requeue had a small race with the epoch TTL; please ensure the TTL check uses a monotonic clock. Also please add a metric for prefixes skipped due to protection.
Priya Raman: Switched TTL logic to monotonic time and added metric kv.protector.skipped_prefixes. Thanks — addressed in e59b0c3.
Liam Patel: Approving pending CI green + canary plan documented. One nit: include a brief rollback step in the runbook.
Priya Raman: Added rollback steps to runbook/regional-failback.md and included the runtime flag stormgate.enabled=false for fast rollback.
ci_checks: Integration tests: flaky on first run (timeout in failback_sim) — rerun passed
Canary smoke checklist: manual verification required post-merge
release_notes: Hotfix: reduce correlated KV evictions during cross-region failback by introducing a bounded admission window (stormgate) and a sparse KV drain protector. Improves stability during reconverge windows and reduces SLO regressions.
changelog: Added stormgate admission controller to moderate reconverge admission bursts
Added sparse KV drain protector to stagger prefix evictions and keep warm caches alive
Updated runbook with rollout and rollback steps
postmerge_actions: Deploy to canary region with stormgate.enabled=true and debug telemetry for 2h
If canary stable, roll out to remaining regions incrementally
Follow-up: schedule automation (ENG-3199) to make protector target list adaptive based on serving heatmap
